note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  - Acute upper lip swelling after eating prawn soup (new food for patient).
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  - Ingestion around 19:00; swelling began ~30 minutes later.
  - Started at left corner of upper lip, progressed to generalized upper lip swelling; worsening/pulsatile sensation.
- ENT symptoms:
  - Throat: Patient reports feeling like breathing is difficult and possibly throat “closing.” No voice change reported. No dysphagia/odynophagia or drooling reported.
  - Nose/eyes: Not reported.
  - Airway/breathing: Dyspnea; unsure about chest tightness; no stridor/noisy breathing reported.
  - Swelling distribution: Upper lip (initially left corner, now more generalized).
  - Ears/neck: Not reported.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  - Prior episode ~1 year ago after late-night Chinese food with swelling and breathing difficulty; treatment details not recalled.
  - Childhood peanut allergy reaction requiring hospital care and an injection per mother’s report.
- Allergies and current medications:
  - Allergies: Peanut (known). Possible new shellfish (prawn) allergy.
  - Medications: Salbutamol inhaler (rescue) – dose/route/frequency not documented. Occasional antihistamines in the past (unspecified); none taken prior to call.
- Any relevant social context:
  - Initially alone; mother arrived during call and is assisting.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution:
  - Patient-reported progressive upper lip swelling. No clinician-documented visual exam.
- Airway/breathing descriptors:
  - Patient-reported difficulty breathing; possible throat tightness. No stridor reported.
- Mental status and associated features:
  - Dizziness reported.
- Vitals and examination findings:
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person:
  - Mother present during/after call.

Assessment:
- Working clinical impression:
  - Suspected anaphylaxis likely triggered by shellfish (prawn) ingestion in a patient with atopy (asthma, peanut allergy).
- Evidence summary:
  - Onset ~30 minutes post-prawn soup; progressive lip angioedema; dyspnea/throat tightness; dizziness; prior severe food allergy reaction in childhood; prior similar episode after restaurant meal.
- DDx (aligned with transcript):
  1) Anaphylaxis due to IgE-mediated shellfish allergy – High likelihood: rapid post-ingestion progression with airway symptoms and dizziness; history of atopy. Opposing evidence: no hives/GI symptoms reported (not required for diagnosis).
  2) IgE-mediated allergic angioedema without full anaphylaxis – Medium: food-triggered lip swelling; however, respiratory symptoms and dizziness favor anaphylaxis.
  3) Contact urticaria/oral allergy syndrome – Low–Medium: initial localized lip symptoms after contact; systemic dyspnea/dizziness argue against.
- No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised:
  - Activate emergency services (999): advised and arranged; mother instructed to call 999 and state “suspected anaphylactic reaction.”
  - Take available antihistamine while awaiting ambulance (advised).
  - Remain with mother; do not stay alone; minimize exertion; sit upright unless lightheaded (then lie supine with legs elevated if safe).
  - Anticipate need for emergency injection (epinephrine) by EMS if indicated.
- Patient/caregiver instructions:
  - Avoid further ingestion of prawns/shellfish and suspected triggering foods.
  - Bring any medication/allergy information to hospital.
- Escalation criteria/red flags while awaiting EMS:
  - Worsening breathing difficulty, voice change/hoarseness, throat closing sensation, stridor, fainting, rapidly increasing tongue/lip swelling.
- Follow-up:
  - Post-hospital follow-up with primary care/ENT/allergy clinic to:
    - Confirm shellfish allergy (formal evaluation).
    - Prescribe and train on epinephrine auto-injector(s) and provide a written anaphylaxis action plan (clinician noted “sort you out with injections”).
    - Review asthma control and consider controller therapy if indicated.
  - Education on strict avoidance of known allergens (peanut and suspected shellfish) and label/restaurant vigilance.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements:
  - Vitals, physical exam findings, presence/absence of urticaria/rash, GI symptoms, wheeze, stridor.
  - Exact antihistamine and salbutamol dosing/frequency; current availability of auto-injector (likely none).
  - Comprehensive allergy list and prior anaphylaxis action plan.
● Conflicts between transcript and DDx:
  - None noted.
● Transcript quality:
  - Conversational with some pauses and disfluency; clinically relevant details captured.
